before: The view pushed into the window (up to 1.45×) on friction, the dropdown, the activity and the intake form, cropping the window at the frame edge and sliding its title bar under the corner mark.
after: The window stays whole in the frame, clear of the corner mark, and only creeps (≤ 3% a second); for emphasis a card lifts out of it with a deeper shadow: the two manual steps, the dropdown, the activity strip, the form.
why: The reference lifts cards out of a window that stays put; the push-ins read as camera zooms on transitions, which K.B's camera rule forbids (both reviews).

before: A new body faded in over the old one ("To do" over "Current process", the form over the board); the months of the plan cross-faded into a doubled grid.
after: The old body slides left and is gone in 0.25 s before the new one comes in from the right; the months turn the same way.
why: Two screens at once read as a glitch (both reviews).

before: The camera's breathing drift showed the stage's own edge as hard lines inside the frame.
after: The stage is 80 px larger than the frame on every side.

before: "With you" was two 52 px chips in the title bar; the "You" chip covered the B, so it read "K.E".
after: A large K.B tile drops in from above and a large "You" rises from below; they meet over the workspace.
why: The line needs a picture, and the brand mark was mangled (both reviews).

before: Automations got a cyan outline and a small corner check.
after: Its card fills with cyan, lifts 1.2×, shows a big check and a small burst; the other modules switch on quietly on "runs".
why: The reference's module switching on is the opening's key moment (fidelity review).

before: The process audit opened on an empty window; a cyan gradient swept across it on "audit".
after: Dashed placeholders for the steps arrive with the window, and a magnifier passes over them on "audit", lighting each one.
why: The sweep looked like a render glitch; the window looked empty (both reviews).

after: The client's phone comes back during the workflow and receives the follow-up email ("Thanks, Jordan! Here's what happens next.").
why: In the reference the phone is a recurring co-star (fidelity review).

before: The Make and n8n tiles landed without names; the AI agent dropped through "Runs today".
after: Each tile shows its name for a second as it lands; the AI agent slides in from the right.
why: Viewers who don't know the logos missed the spoken names; a collision (both reviews).

before: "Copy" and "Paste" were small keys at the top edge, struck by one cyan line that missed "Paste".
after: Two large keys, each struck out in red on "paste", then gone.
why: Cyan read as a highlight, not a "no" (both reviews).

before: The K.B avatar slid along the team row, over "4 members" and through two people.
after: The team makes room, K.B takes the seat, and the count changes to 5 as it lands; the messages fill the channel from the top.
why: A collision, and an empty channel (both reviews).

before: The monthly plan had a solid navy and a solid cyan bar across every week; the New feature chip covered the dates.
after: Thin Hosting and Maintenance lines with a legend; the New feature chip sits inside its day, which lights up; "K.B · on call" is pinned to the month on "we stay on".
why: The heaviest frame of the film, and "we stay on" showed an empty calendar (both reviews).

before: The loop drew over the leaving calendar, grew until "Diagnose" was clipped, then shrank 82% into the logo.
after: The plan leaves first; the road draws from Diagnose to each station before it is named; the loop grows only 3%; it fades before the logo comes in.
why: Overlap, clipping, and a zoom on a transition (both reviews).

before: Green fills (Sent, Live, Running) and green check marks.
after: Navy buttons and pills with a cyan dot or a cyan check.
why: Off-brand, and white on green failed contrast (craft review).

before: The end card was the logo and a navy button, arriving 2 s before the end; the shapes kept spinning.
after: The logo, "Talk to K.B." built word by word on the voice, and a cyan "Book a Free Discovery Call" button; the shapes ease to a stop.
why: The reference's button is in the action colour and echoes the spoken line; a calm sign-off (both reviews).
